audit.why: HARD at 7/10 fits 46.59% over 264 games. Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against a champion whose longest pre-6 tool is a 650 charge, and Hop exits the one angle she can approach from. The lane is a poke lane she survives rather than contests.
audit.corrected: Difficulty and the Gnar-favoured early chart kept.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page treats Hop as an always-available escape ('his hop E exits every approach angle') and gives no ultimate cooldowns at level 6.
audit.why: Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s — one of the longest mobility cooldowns in the lane, and longer than Arctic Assault's 18s at rank 1. A spent Hop is a 22-second window where he cannot leave, which is the single most actionable spike in the matchup and the page never mentions it. Likewise GNAR! is 90/60/30s against Glacial Prison's 120/105/90 — he gets more ultimates than you, so trading R for R is a losing exchange.
audit.corrected: Hop's 22 seconds written into whys[1] and the early block; the ultimate cooldown asymmetry written into whys[4] and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four naming errors. (a) 'his Hyper passive' — Hyper is his W in Mini form; the passive is Rage Gene. (b) 'a comet into him' and 'Throw your comet' — Glacial Prison is a bola, not a comet. (c) 'Force Mega-Gnar transforms during Permafrost's cooldown window' — Permafrost is 1.5s, there is no such window. (d) 'your passive Permafrost resistances' fuses Permafrost with Fury of the North's Frost Armor.
audit.why: Riot: Rage Gene is the passive ('While in combat Gnar generates Rage. At maximum Rage his next ability will transform him'); Hyper is the Mini form of W, 'Gnar's attacks and spells hype him up, dealing bonus damage and granting him Move Speed', and Wallop is the Mega form that stuns. Riot on Glacial Prison: 'Sejuani throws her bola'. Riot on Permafrost: 1.5s cooldown, fires at maximum Frost stacks — the resource that gates it is your stacks, not a cooldown. Riot on Fury of the North: the resistances are Frost Armor, an out-of-combat buff.
audit.corrected: Rage Gene, Hyper, Wallop, bola and Frost Armor all named correctly; the fabricated Permafrost window replaced with a Frost-stack condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names the Rage bar as the matchup-defining 'cooldown' and gives no ability timers at all.
audit.why: The Rage bar is a real read and worth keeping, but it is not a cooldown. The countable numbers are Hop 22/19.5/17/14.5/12s, Boomerang Throw 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Wallop 7s and GNAR! 90/60/30s.
audit.corrected: Hop's 22 seconds made the punishable window, with the Rage bar kept as the second read.

audit.why: The late block already carries the one mechanic that matters here — GNAR! only stuns enemies thrown into a wall, so the counterplay is standing away from terrain. Riot: 'Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.' That is correctly stated and was kept.

edits.after: At Level 1 Gnar wins everything — Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 before you can apply a single Frost stack, and you have no way to bridge that. Take W, last-hit cleanly from a safe distance, and accept that any step toward him is poke you cannot answer. When he double-taps Boomerang, watch the Rage Gene bar — a near-full Gnar is about to transform, and that is the one window you never trade into. At Level 2 your Q gives you a threat angle, but Hop simply leaps him backward out of it. At Level 3 your full Q-W-E chain is live and so is his Wallop-into-Hop kite pattern; he wins the extended trade because poke accumulates faster than Frost stacks can be delivered in one clean burst. The number to hold onto is Hop's cooldown: 22 seconds at rank 1, and while it is down he cannot leave.
edits.before: At Level 1 Gnar wins everything — his Boomerang reaches you before you can apply a single Frost stack, and you have no way to bridge the gap. Take W, last-hit cleanly from safe distance, and accept that any step toward him is poke damage you cannot immediately answer. The moment he double-taps Boomerang to stack Rage, note the bar — a near-full Rage Gnar is about to transform and that is the one window you absolutely do not trade into. At Level 2 your Q gives you a threat angle, but Gnar's hop means any Q you throw telegraphs your path and he simply leaps backward. At Level 3 your full Q-W-E chain is live, but so is his Wallop-into-hop kite pattern; he wins the extended trade at this stage because poke damage accumulates faster than your stacking Frost can be delivered in one clean burst.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are your counter-intuitive ownership window: Gnar is most dangerous near full Rage, but Rage also depletes in Mini form — when he is Rage-empty and Mini he has to commit to extended trades to rebuild it, and that is when Q into both W arcs into Permafrost lands with maximum impact. Watch the Rage Gene bar like a second HP bar. At Level 6 the matchup becomes genuinely contested: Mega Gnar and Glacial Prison are both long-range CC, and whoever lands first dictates it. Throw the bola while he is Mini with Rage draining — catching him mid-Hop is the kill setup. Never throw R at a full-Rage Gnar near your tower; GNAR! into a wall is a death sentence, and his ultimate is 90 seconds to your 120.
edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are your counter-intuitive ownership window: Gnar is at his most dangerous when Rage is nearly full, but his Rage also depletes in Mini form — when he is Rage-empty and Mini, he commits to extended trades to rebuild the bar, and that is when your Q-into-W double-strike-into-E stun lands with maximum impact. Watch the Rage bar like a second HP bar. At Level 6 the matchup becomes genuinely contested: his Mega-Gnar and your Glacial Prison are both long-range CC threats, and whoever lands first dictates the outcome. Throw your comet when he is in Mini form with Rage depleting — a mid-air hit during his hop is the kill setup. Never throw R into a full-Rage Gnar standing near your tower; his GNAR! into wall is a death sentence.

edits.after: With two tank items the Frost Armor from Fury of the North makes you functionally unkillable in a 1v1, but Gnar's value at this stage is teamfight utility — his AOE Mega stun creates the same chaos your own R does. The key is positioning: stand far enough from terrain that GNAR! cannot bounce you into a wall, since only enemies that hit one are stunned, then answer with Glacial Prison the instant he lands from the throw. In teamfights you are the superior initiator — your bola can open from fog, his ultimate needs a transformation he cannot always time. Punish objectives and river fights where he cannot kite freely; stay out of enclosed geometry unless you are the one starting it.
edits.before: With two tank items your passive Permafrost resistances make you functionally unkillable in a 1v1, but Gnar's value at this stage is team-fight utility — his AOE Mega stun into your own R creates the same chaos he does on your team. The key is positioning: stand far enough from the wall that his GNAR! toss cannot bounce you into three allies, then answer with Glacial Prison the instant he lands from the throw. In teamfights you are the superior engage initiator — your R can open from fog of war, his requires a transformation he cannot always time. Punish objectives and river fights where he cannot kite freely; stay out of enclosed geometry unless you are initiating.

notes: The highest-value number on this page was missing entirely: Hop is 22/19.5/17/14.5/12 seconds. The page repeatedly frames Gnar as un-catchable because of his Hop, when in fact his escape is on a longer cooldown than Sejuani's engage at rank 1 — that inverts the advice from 'never approach' to 'approach the moment Hop is spent'. Three fabricated or misattributed names were also fixed: 'Hyper passive' (Hyper is the Mini form of W; the passive is Rage Gene), 'comet' for Glacial Prison (Riot calls it a bola — this fabrication appears on several Sejuani pages and is worth a global grep), and 'Permafrost's cooldown window' (Permafrost is 1.5s; the gate is Frost stacks). Also note the ultimate asymmetry the page never priced: GNAR! is 90/60/30 against Glacial Prison's 120/105/90, so he can afford to trade ultimates and you cannot.
